guards.what: EV-3: CalculateVars' `Gold = base.Rng.NextInt(61, 100)` (DenseVegetation.cs:37) rolls on the sim's shared run RNG (`self.rng`) where C# rolls on the per-event `base.Rng`
guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-3, one verdict at every site (rule 3). Each C# EventModel gets its own Rng seeded from the run seed + event id, and the sim already models it: Event.__init__ builds `self.event_rng` from make_event_rng(seed, ID) for string-seeded runs (events/base.py:84-88), and 6 modules branch on it. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/event_probes.py eventrng`): 28 of the 34 event modules that roll anything roll ONLY on `self.rng`. LIVE for the parity path that the conformance harness grades -- a shared-rng draw both takes a number the game never takes off that stream and fails to advance the event stream, desyncing the rest of the run. In legacy (RL) mode both are the same random.Random, so the observable is parity-only -- which is an exercised sim mode, not an unreachable one.

guards.what: `foreach (Player player in runState.Players)` HP gate in IsAllowed (DenseVegetation.cs:47-53)
guards.rationale: multiplayer-only: the C# predicate is `runState.Players.All(p => ...)`, a quantifier over the party. The sim is single-player, so the quantifier collapses to the one player's clause, which the sim implements exactly. Out of scope per the shared contract's multiplayer waiver.

C# routes event damage through CreatureCmd.Damage, whose Hook.ShouldDie / Hook.AfterPreventingDeath pass runs over RunState.IterateHookListeners (RunState.cs:545-596), which yields the POTION BELT outside combat; RunState.lose_hp (run.py:294-302) just subtracts
guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-1, one verdict at all 18 lose_hp sites (rule 3). Fairy in a Bottle (FairyInABottle.cs:33-45: ShouldDie false for its owner, AfterPreventingDeath heals to max(MaxHp*0.3, 1)) IS ported (potions.py:1222-1250) and IS in the reward pool (potion_pools.py:49), but the sim's copy returns early when `self.combat is None` (potions.py:1246-1248) and is only registered as a listener by CombatState (combat.py:164-166), so it is inert during an event. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/event_probes.py lethal`): a run at 5 HP holding a belt Fairy that loses 15 HP ends DEAD at hp=-10 with the Fairy still in the belt; the game ends alive at 24 HP with the Fairy consumed. LIVE -- both sides ported and reachable, and the divergence ends the run. Secondary: run.lose_hp does not clamp at 0 either, so the sim carries negative HP.
